title: Her Name Was Never Recorded. Her Face Survived 171 Years #shorts
description:
Sixth-plate daguerreotype, hand-colored, c. 1855. Stamped on the brass mat: F. Grice, Rochester, New York. Her name was never recorded - the plate was never signed, and the archive catalogued it simply as [Unidentified young woman, half-length portrait, facing front].

A daguerreotype was made on a silvered copper sheet, and the exposure took tens of seconds. That is why nobody smiles on these plates: they simply could not hold one that long.

171 years of oxidation bloom, scratches and silver mirroring, removed layer by layer.

Source: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, DAG no. 1502. Public Domain. No known restrictions on publication.
Restored with AI. The face and the sheer yoke are reconstructed, not recovered - the original plate is too faded to carry fine detail. Dress, hands and background are the plate itself, cleaned classically.
